claim_model.bytes: Parse the envelope and frame format, verify lengths, CRC32, SHA-256 and sequence continuity; truncate only an incomplete tail and reject every complete corruption.
claim_model.history: Serve original history consumers: /changes pages carrying commit identities from the change floor, and point-in-time reads at or above the version floor.

history_scope.commits_and_changes: commit identities and change pages are available from the journal base
history_scope.snapshots_only: point-in-time reads within the version floor work; no commit identity or change page for any earlier sequence is available
history_scope.snapshots_plus_new_changes: point-in-time reads work and change records start at the restore base; earlier commit identities are unavailable

claim_model.important: A sample can pass bytes and state while failing part of history: R9-bare keeps snapshots but exposes no commit identities or change pages, and R9-cont10 adds change records only from its restore base. A digest-valid image can fail state (X09..X13). No single pass bit means semantic compatibility, and equal format hashes do not.
claim_model.state: Reconstruct catalogue, index definitions, version chains, tombstones and logical constraints at the head sequence.

control_recipes.G1-single-tx/G4-four-tx: Four distinct rows inserted either in one commit or four commits.
control_recipes.T7-twin: The source recipe replayed independently in a fresh directory. Transaction ids are random, so the checkpoint bytes match while journal identities do not.

V0-novacuum.relation_to_source: Same schema, transaction boundaries and row values as the source; the single differing operation is the vacuum target (0 instead of 5).

alternatives_considered.every_anchor_checkpoint: Storing a checkpoint at each of sequences 1..10 plus every journal prefix would be about 10 images and 10 journals; the four images and eight journals kept here preserve every discriminating difference at roughly half the bytes.
alternatives_considered.latest_only: One image plus one full journal is smaller but cannot represent the pre-vacuum horizon, so the most important retention control disappears.

journals_kept: one commit versus four commits (four rows)
coverage.reconstructed_not_stored: Prefixes are sliced from the source journal; empty restored journals are rebuilt as a 16-byte header. No prefix is stored twice.
coverage.why_not_latest_only: A single latest image erases the version floor transition, tombstone chains, the vacuum record and every commit identity. R9-cont10 would become indistinguishable from C9-suffix10 and X16-X19 could not replay.

cross_checks.detail: C7-prefix and T7-twin share checkpoint sha256 b55359da7dd3619afbbe815ad477544e8bc88cebe1877b0f005a75b1515d6cf6 while their history digests differ.
Two independent runs of the same recipe expose different transaction ids at every commit sequence.
The source at sequence 9, the bare restore and the restored continuation agree on rows and version floor 5 while the change floor is 0 for the source and 9 for both restored instances.
A restored instance still answers at=5 and at=8 while /changes?after=4 returns 410.
Sequence 10 carries the source transaction id in C9-suffix10 and a different id in R9-cont10.
Identical sequence, record count and head rows; only the vacuum target moves the version floor from 0 to 5 and changes which old snapshots are answerable.
One transaction or four produce identical rows while commit identity and history differ.
Three trailing bytes are truncated and state/history match J10-full.
Both prefix pairs replay to exactly their image sequence with no suffix.
X09..X13 all carry a recomputed valid digest and still fail state validation.
The real binary rejects every controlled corruption the oracle rejects.

purpose: Separate three claims about a new reader: it can recognize the bytes, it can recover the relational state, and it can still serve the original history consumers. Backup restore and change replay must jointly explain commit identity and retention watermarks; equal directories or equal current queries do not imply continuous history.

rebuild.determinism: Transaction ids are random. Regeneration changes ids and therefore journal and history digests, so only within-run cross-checks and semantic digests are stable. The manifest records the generating binary digest and time.

retention_model.change_floor: earliest after cursor accepted by /changes; carried by the journal header base
retention_model.rule: The floors are independent. A restore moves the change floor to the image sequence while preserving the version floor, so old snapshots stay readable after old change cursors are already gone. A reader that derives one floor from the other is wrong in both directions.
retention_model.version_floor: oldest at accepted by a point-in-time query; carried by the image horizon and advanced only by a vacuum record
